fields.expected: I'm an undergraduate at Johns Hopkins studying Applied Mathematics & Statistics and Economics, and most of my work has been building machine learning systems that have to hold up against real users and real failure modes. Right now I work on the machine learning core of an anomaly-detection and alert-prioritization system at Summer Atlantic Capital / SAC Nexus, where I own the event-ingestion pipeline, a versioned FastAPI detection service, and the CI scaffold. The modeling is temporal sequence modeling over event streams with RNN and Transformer-style approaches, anomaly scoring, and a learning-to-rank layer, plus a retrieval-augmented explanation layer so an analyst can understand why something was flagged. The thing I've spent most of my time on is not raw model performance but alert volume and explanation quality, since a detector that floods a queue creates a second problem instead of solving the first. Before that I built an evaluation framework at Intelehealth comparing LLM-generated clinical outputs against a 4,169-case standard using stratified sampling to surface systematic failure modes. That work is why I care about evaluation as its own engineering problem, which is what draws me to building AI systems inside a production trading platform like Tradeweb.
